Lists the boleto transactions of your company, most recent first, so you can
reconcile boleto receivables and payments against your own records.

A transaction is either a `BOLETO_IN` — a boleto your payer paid — or a
`BOLETO_OUT` — a boleto your company paid. All monetary values are in cents.

`value` is the amount that actually moved, which for a boleto paid after the
due date is above the emitted amount in `charge.value` because of interest
and fine. `finesValue` and `interestsValue` split that difference, as charged
by the bank, so you can reconcile an overdue boleto without recomputing it
from the charge settings. Each is absent when there was none, so a boleto
paid on time carries neither.

Two independent date ranges are offered because they answer different
questions: `start`/`end` filter by when the transaction was created, and
`settledStart`/`settledEnd` by when Woovi credited the amount to your
account. Both dates come back on every item.

Requires the `BOLETO_TRANSACTION_GET_LIST` scope on the application.

Endpoint to create a new Charge for a customer.

## Split

You can split the value of a charge across other accounts by sending the
`splits` array in the request body. Each item accepts:

  - `value`: amount in cents that will be split to the destination.
  - `pixKey`: Pix key of the account that will receive this split.
  - `splitType`: how the split is processed — one of `SPLIT_INTERNAL_TRANSFER`,
    `SPLIT_SUB_ACCOUNT` or `SPLIT_PARTNER`.
    [See how each split type is processed](https://developers.openpix.com.br/docs/splits/split-introduction).

See the *Charge with Split Internal Transfer* and *Charge with Split Subaccounts*
request body examples below for the full payload shape.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Uploads a file and returns its metadata with a pre-signed download URL.
The file is sent as `multipart/form-data` on the `file` field, together
with the `purpose` that describes what the file is for.

Send exactly one file per request, of one of the supported content types,
up to 10 MiB (`10485760` bytes).

When you send a `correlationID`, repeating the request with the same
`correlationID` and `purpose` returns the file already stored (`200`)
instead of uploading a second copy, so the request is safe to retry.
Without a `correlationID` one is generated for you and every call stores a
new file.

The `url` in the response is temporary and expires at `urlExpiresAt`; ask
for the file again to get a fresh one.

item.name: Generate the payment book (carnê) of a subscription

request.name: Generate the payment book (carnê) of a subscription

description.content:
Builds the payment book (carnê) of a subscription as a PDF — one slip per
installment, in a single request, up to the `month`/`year` you ask for.

**Only for `type: RECURRENT` subscriptions.** Pix Automático
(`PIX_RECURRING`) has no payment book: there the payer's bank executes each
charge on its own date, so the charges cannot be brought forward into a
document. Asking for the payment book of a Pix Automático subscription is
answered with `400`.

A subscription's future installments do not exist as charges yet — each one
is created close to its own due date. Printing a booklet brings that forward.

**The call is synchronous and creates every missing charge in the period.**
Nothing is queued and there is no ticket to poll: it walks the installments
up to the cutoff you asked for, creates the charge of each one that does not
have it, and answers only once the PDF is ready. **Response time is therefore
much longer than a normal call, and grows with the number of charges to
create** — a long booklet asked for the first time is the worst case, because
none of its installments exist yet. Raise your client's timeout before asking
for a long period; the default in most HTTP libraries is too short for this.

Those charges are real: they show on your statement, fire the usual webhooks
when paid, and follow your account's commercial terms, including any boleto
issuing fee that applies to it. So treat it as a write even though it is a
`GET`: do not put it behind a blind retry, a link prefetch or a monitoring
check, and ask only for the period you are going to hand to the customer.

`month` and `year` are required and reach at most the end of next year. There
is no default — the pair decides how many charges are created, so the caller
states it.

Repeating the request is safe: an installment that already has a charge does
not get a second one, so a reprint costs nothing and widening the window
creates only the difference. That is also the recovery if your client times
out — call the same URL again.

The booklet carries a slip for each in-range installment that is still open.
Installments already paid or expired are left out, so it never invites paying
the same one twice — which is why the slip count can be lower than the number
of installments in the period.

query.description: (Required) Last month the booklet reaches, `1`–`12`. Required.

(Required) Last year the booklet reaches. Required, and limited to the current year
or the next one — a later year is answered with `400`, it is not
truncated to the ceiling. A month/year already past is accepted and
simply yields fewer slips.

item.name: Read the BC Protege+ gate of an account register

request.name: Read the BC Protege+ gate of an account register

description.content:
BC Protege+ is a Banco Central registry. A holder who enables it blocks
the opening of accounts in their name, so while it is active for the
company CNPJ or for any active ADMIN CPF, Woovi cannot open the account.

The gate requires the CNPJ and every active ADMIN to be `AUTHORIZED`.
Anything else blocks, the absence of a record included. `blocking` lists
every scope currently blocking, not just the first one.

Only the merchant can resolve a block: they disable BC Protege+ at Banco
Central, you call `POST /api/v1/kyc/bc-protection/resend`, Woovi
re-queries, and the record turns `AUTHORIZED`. No Woovi endpoint or
operator action can force it.

When `applicable` is `false` (the company lacks
`BC_PROTECTION_KYC_AUTHORIZE`, or the account is international) the gate
never blocks and the rest of the body is informational.

Required scope: `KYC_BC_PROTECTION_GET`.

query.description:
(Required) Identifies the account register: the `correlationID` sent to
`POST /api/v1/kyc/onboarding`, or the register's CNPJ (digits that form
a valid CNPJ are looked up as a tax ID). Always scoped to the
authenticated company — a register of another company is not found.

item.name: Re-run the BC Protege+ verification for one tax ID

request.name: Re-run the BC Protege+ verification for one tax ID

description.content:
Call this after the merchant says they disabled the protection at Banco
Central. It re-runs the Banco Central query (SRC0001) for that tax ID.

The answer is asynchronous: `202` means the query was accepted, not that
the situation changed. Read `GET /api/v1/kyc/bc-protection` again (or
wait for the `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_STEP_UPDATED` webhook) to see the result.

Rate limited to one resend per hour per (account register, tax ID). A
resend inside the window answers `429` with `nextResendAt` in the body.
The first query on a register is not a resend and never consumes the
cooldown.

Required scope: `KYC_BC_PROTECTION_POST`.

item.name: Attach company documents to an account register

request.name: Attach company documents to an account register

description.content:
Company documents are sent as files uploaded first. Two calls:

1. `POST /api/v1/files` (multipart) with `purpose=ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENT`.
   Keep the `id` it returns.
2. This endpoint, with that id as `documents[].fileId` and the document
   `type`.

A `fileId` must belong to the calling company **and** have been uploaded
with purpose `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENT`; any other file is not found.
Every `fileId` is resolved before anything is written, so a request with
one unknown file attaches none of them.

Accepted while the register waits on the merchant (`DRAFT`, `PENDING`)
and while compliance has an open request for information. A document
that answers a requested item clears it, and the request closes once
nothing is left.

Required scope: `KYC_DOCUMENTS_POST`.

item.name: Create a Pix authentication ceremony for a representative

request.name: Create a Pix authentication ceremony for a representative

description.content:
Mints the Pix charge an ADMIN representative pays to prove they hold a
bank account under their own CPF. The charge is created with
`ensureSameTaxID`, so the Pix arrangement itself refuses a payment whose
payer CPF differs from the representative CPF. The amount is refunded on
every terminal outcome.

Requires the feature `PIX_AUTHENTICATION_KYC` on the company that owns
the register. In sandbox the ceremony cannot be completed (it needs a
real Pix payment), so the gate is dropped there.

**Idempotent by ceremony, not by request.** Calling it again while a
ceremony is open returns the same `txId` and `brCode` instead of minting
a second charge. A representative already verified answers `200` with
`result: MATCHED` and no `brCode` — treat that as success.

Accepted while the register is `PENDING`, or later while an open request
for information asks this representative for a Pix authentication.

Required scope: `KYC_PIX_AUTHENTICATION_POST`.

item.name: Read the result of a Pix authentication ceremony

request.name: Read the result of a Pix authentication ceremony

description.content:
Reconciles the ceremony and reports its result. This read is what settles
it: a payment that landed since the last poll is matched here.

Switch on `result`, not on `status`:

| result | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| `UNVERIFIED` | No payment settled yet | Keep polling until `dueDate` |
| `MATCHED` | The payer CPF is the representative CPF | Done for this representative |
| `MISMATCH` | A payment settled but the payer failed a check | Create a new ceremony |

`MISMATCH` covers three failures — the payer CPF differs, the paying
institution failed the ISPB check, or the payer could not be resolved.
All three consume the ceremony, so the representative needs a new QR.

Suggested cadence (same as the hosted wizard): poll every 5 seconds,
back off to 10, 20 and 40 seconds on consecutive transport errors, and
stop after four consecutive failures.

Required scope: `KYC_PIX_AUTHENTICATION_GET`.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Creates a new KYC onboarding for a merchant. Returns a link that should be sent
to the merchant so they can fill in their registration data.

The register starts in `PENDING`, with the representatives enriched from the
CNPJ. Instead of (or besides) sending the link, your integration can drive every
step over the API — `POST /api/v1/kyc/documents`, `/api/v1/kyc/representatives`,
`/api/v1/kyc/pix-authentication`, `/api/v1/kyc/bc-protection` — and finish with
`POST /api/v1/kyc/onboarding/submit`. The `correlationID` sent here is how every
one of those endpoints addresses the register.

The API is idempotent by `correlationID`. If the same `correlationID` is sent again
for the same company, the API returns the existing onboarding link (200 OK) instead
of creating a new one.

The fields `officialName`, `tradeName` and `representatives[].name` are automatically
populated via data enrichment when available. You do not need to send them in the request.

`website` and `businessDescription` can be pre-filled by the caller. In the Brazilian
flow `businessDescription` is the only field gating the `COMPANY_DATA` onboarding step,
so sending it here lets the merchant skip that step of the wizard. On an idempotent
replay both fields are only written when still empty — data typed by the applicant is
never overwritten.

If `redirectUrl` is provided, the merchant is automatically redirected to that URL
5 seconds after completing the onboarding flow (terminal states: submitted, approved,
or rejected). The `redirectUrl` is bound to the onboarding link at creation time and
cannot be changed later — subsequent idempotent calls will return the original value.

item.name: Submit an account register for compliance review

request.name: Submit an account register for compliance review

description.content:
The last step of the full-API onboarding: sends a register created by
`POST /api/v1/kyc/onboarding` into compliance analysis (`IN_REVIEW`).
The hosted link has its own submit on its review screen; this is the
equivalent when your integration drives every step over the API.

Only a register waiting on the merchant (`DRAFT` or `PENDING`) can be
submitted. A register in any other status (`APPROVED`, `REJECTED`,
`CREATING`, `FAILED`) is refused with `409` and code
`STATUS_NOT_SUBMITTABLE`; concurrent calls move it into review once.

Every gate runs on the server. Submission is refused with `409` while
any of them is open, and `code` says which one:

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `MISSING_PIX_AUTHENTICATION` | An active ADMIN has no `MATCHED` Pix ceremony (only when the company has `PIX_AUTHENTICATION_KYC`) |
| `BC_PROTECTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED` | The CNPJ or an active ADMIN is not `AUTHORIZED` at Banco Central |
| `MISSING_REPRESENTATIVE_DOCUMENTS` | An active ADMIN lacks the selfie (`PICTURE`) or a valid identity document |
| `PENDING_REQUESTED_DOCUMENTS` | Compliance asked for documents that were not sent |
| `PENDING_BC_PROTEGE` | The only pending request is the BC Protege+ one |
| `STATUS_NOT_SUBMITTABLE` | The register is not in `DRAFT`/`PENDING` (already decided, or being provisioned) |

**The Pix ceremony blocks here and does not block the hosted link.** The
link lets an unverified register into review and enforces the ceremony
afterwards; an API integration has no later screen to send the merchant
back to, so it is enforced up front.

Idempotent: a register already `IN_REVIEW` answers `200` with its
existing `inReviewAt` and re-runs nothing, so a timed-out call is safe to
retry. On success Woovi sends the `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_IN_REVIEW` webhook,
and later `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_APPROVED`, `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_REJECTED` or
`ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENTS_REQUESTED`.

Required scope: `KYC_ONBOARDING_SUBMIT_POST`.

item.name: Add a representative, optionally with its documents

request.name: Add a representative, optionally with its documents

description.content:
Adds a partner to a register that is still `DRAFT` or `PENDING`: the
person, then their identity and selfie as the ids of files uploaded
first through `POST /api/v1/files` (purpose `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENT`,
same company).

Every `fileId` is resolved before the partner is written: an unknown
file adds nothing. A file the synchronous quality check refuses (blurred,
cropped) comes back in `rejectedDocuments` and can be resent through
`POST /api/v1/kyc/representatives/documents`.

A CPF already active on the register answers `409`. A CPF on a
deactivated representative reactivates that row (`200`,
`reactivated: true`) instead of creating a second one. A MEI has a single
owner. Domestic registers require a valid CPF.

`type: ADMIN` (the default) owes the Pix authentication and the BC

item.name: Send the email code to a ceremony admin

request.name: Send the email code to a ceremony admin

description.content:
Sends a 6-digit code to the email stored on the representative, the one
sent in `email` to `POST /api/v1/kyc/representatives` or on the
onboarding. Confirming it through
`POST /api/v1/kyc/representatives/email-code/verify` proves the admin
holds that address.

Required only when the company that owns the register has the feature
`KYC_REPRESENTATIVE_EMAIL_OTP`, and only for the administrators the Pix
authentication also requires (the target administrators, when the
register has any). Until each of them confirms, the submit answers `409`
with `MISSING_REPRESENTATIVE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION`. Changing the email
after the confirmation asks for a new one.

A code lives 10 minutes. Calling this again while it is live sends the
same code again instead of a new one. Between two calls there is a
30-second cooldown; each admin gets 3 codes an hour, each register 10,
and one address 6 a day. Every refusal of that kind is a `200` with an
`outcome`, not an error:

| outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CODE_SENT` | The code went out by email: a new one, or the live one again |
| `ALREADY_SENT` | Nothing new was spent: the code went out less than 30 seconds ago, or a code the mailer did not take was delivered again |
| `ALREADY_VERIFIED` | The current email is already confirmed |
| `SAME_AS_ACCOUNT_USER` | The email is the one the account user already confirmed; nothing to do |
| `COOLDOWN` | Wait 30 seconds since the last code |
| `SEND_LIMIT_REACHED` | No codes left for now |
| `BLOCKED` | 3 wrong codes; no new code for 24 hours after the last one |
| `TRY_AGAIN` | A concurrent call won, or the send limiter is unavailable; call again |

Required scope: `KYC_REPRESENTATIVES_POST`.

item.name: Read the request for information of an account register

request.name: Read the request for information of an account register

description.content:
When compliance needs more from the merchant it opens a request for
information (RFI) and sends the `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENTS_REQUESTED`
webhook. This endpoint returns what was asked (`rfi`), what is still
pending for the company and for each representative, how each pending
item is answered (`answeredBy`), and the hosted `link` that answers it.

There are two ways to answer, and they can be mixed:

- **API** — `POST /api/v1/kyc/rfi` with the fileIds of files uploaded
  through `POST /api/v1/files` (purpose `ACCOUNT_REGISTER_DOCUMENT`).
- **Link** — send the merchant to `link`. It is the only way to answer an
  item whose `answeredBy` is `LINK` (a website, a business description, a
  tax ID regularization).

| answeredBy | answered through |
|---|---|
| `FILE` | `POST /api/v1/kyc/rfi` (or the documents endpoints) |
| `PIX_AUTHENTICATION` | `POST /api/v1/kyc/pix-authentication` |
| `BC_PROTECTION` | `POST /api/v1/kyc/bc-protection/resend`, once the merchant disabled it |
| `LINK` | the hosted `link` |

The request closes (`status: RESOLVED`, webhook
`ACCOUNT_REGISTER_RFI_RESOLVED`) once nothing is pending.

Required scope: `KYC_RFI_GET`.

query.description:
(Required) Identifies the account register: the `correlationID` sent to
`POST /api/v1/kyc/onboarding`, or the register's CNPJ (digits that form

item.name: Ask to raise the limits of an account

request.name: Ask to raise the limits of an account

description.content:
Opens a limit-increase request for one of your accounts. It is created with
`status: IN_REVIEW`; poll
[`GET /api/v1/limits/request/{limitRequestId}`](#operation/getLimitRequest)
until it becomes `APPROVED` (with `approvedLimits`) or `REJECTED`.

## Upload the supporting document FIRST

A limit request is never accepted without at least one document justifying
it, and the document does **not** travel in this request. It is a two-step
flow, and the order matters:

**Step 1 — upload the file.** Send it to
[`POST /api/v1/files`](#operation/uploadFile) as `multipart/form-data`,
with **`purpose=ACCOUNT_LIMIT_REQUEST`**. That endpoint needs the
`FILE_POST` scope and accepts `application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`
and `image/webp` up to 10 MiB. Keep the `file.id` it returns.

```
curl -X POST https://api.woovi.com/api/v1/files \
  -H 'Authorization: <your AppID>' \
  -F 'purpose=ACCOUNT_LIMIT_REQUEST' \
  -F 'file=@faturamento.pdf'
```

**Step 2 — open the request with that id**, in `documents[].fileId`:

```
curl -X POST https://api.woovi.com/api/v1/limits/request \
  -H 'Authorization: <your AppID>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"companyBankAccountId":"65f1c2e9a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
       "pixDayLimit":5000000,
       "pixNightLimit":200000,
       "documents":[{"fileId":"68c7d0a1f0b2c3d4e5f60718"}]}'
```

A `fileId` is only accepted when the file belongs to **your** company and
was uploaded with `purpose=ACCOUNT_LIMIT_REQUEST`. Anything else — a file
of another company, another purpose, or an id that does not exist —
answers `400` and no request is created. Uploading the file with the wrong
purpose is the most common cause of that `400`: upload it again with the
right one, you do not need to delete the first.

## The limits you send

Limits are in cents and use the same field names as
[`GET /api/v1/limits/{accountId}`](#operation/getAccountLimits), so read
the current values there, raise the ones you need, and send them here.
`pixDayLimit` and `pixNightLimit` are always required. No field may be
**below** its current value, and at least one must be **above** it —
otherwise the request is a `400`.

Only one request per account can be `IN_REVIEW` at a time; a second one
answers `409` while the first is still being analysed.

Retrieves the most recent account limits configured for a given bank account,
including the stablecoin (`stableIn*` / `stableOut*`) and TED (`tedIn*` /
`tedOut*` / `tedRefundReceived*` / `tedRefundSent*`) limits.
Only the public-safe fields are returned; internal-only fields are stripped from the response.
Fields with no cap configured are omitted from the response.

The response also carries a real-time `usage` block: how much of each
limit has already been consumed in the current window, computed from the
same limits document plus the live counters (no extra lookups). See
`AccountLimitUsage` for the full contract — in short, `totalLimit: null`
means unlimited and `totalLimit: 0` means blocked, and those two states

Endpoint to request a payment. Supports four payment types: Pix Key (`PIX_KEY`), QR Code (`QR_CODE`), Manual (`MANUAL`), and Boleto (`BOLETO`).

For QR Code payments, the system decodes the BR Code string and extracts the destination and value automatically.

For Boleto payments, send `type: "BOLETO"` and the `boletoBarcode`. The amount, due date and beneficiary are resolved from the boleto, so `value` and destination are not sent in the body. Validate the barcode first with `POST /api/v1/boleto/validate`.

Set `autoApprove: true` to create and immediately approve the payment in a single call, returning the enriched response with transaction and destination data. Without this flag, the payment is created in `CREATED` status and can be approved later via `POST /api/v1/payment/approve`.

item.name: Create a Pix authentication for a CPF or CNPJ

request.name: Create a Pix authentication for a CPF or CNPJ

description.content:
Mints the R$ 0,01 Pix the payer must pay from a bank account under the
declared document, and charges `PIX_AUTH_FEE`.

**Idempotent by `correlationID`.** Posting the same `correlationID` and
`taxID` while it is open answers `200` with the same Pix authentication,
`brCode` and `hostedUrl`, and charges nothing again. A `correlationID`

request.name: Create the withdraw Pix key of the account

description.content:
Registers a new Pix key as a withdraw key of the company and sets it as the
withdraw Pix key of the account linked to the AppID.

**This endpoint is not enabled by default.** Ask support to enable the withdraw
Pix key API for your account; without it the endpoint returns 403.

The Pix key is checked on the DICT and its holder must match the account holder.
Pix keys of Woovi accounts can not be used.

If the Pix key is already a withdraw key of the company, use
`PUT /api/v1/pix-keys/withdraw` to select it. If the key was created but could
not be selected, retry with `PUT /api/v1/pix-keys/withdraw`.

`ID` names the transaction, and what it is depends on `ReceiptType`:

| ReceiptType  | ID                                                                      |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `pix-in`     | The `endToEndId` of the Pix you received (`E…`)                         |
| `pix-out`    | The `endToEndId` of the Pix you sent (`E…`)                             |
| `pix-refund` | The `endToEndId` of the refund itself, its return id (`D…`), not the one of the Pix it refunds |
| `ted-in`     | The `correlationID` or `nuop` of a TED you received (`TED_IN`)          |
| `ted-out`    | The `correlationID` or `nuop` of a TED you sent (`TED_OUT`)             |

types, a ted type only finds TEDs of its kind: a TED sent asked as `ted-in` is a `404`. Only
transactions of the company behind the AppID are found.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Creates a stablecoin deposit (PIX-in to stable-out) for a company. The deposit
converts a BRL amount (in cents) into the requested stablecoin on the chosen network
and returns a quote with the applied fees.

There are two fee models, and the amount field you send picks one:
  - `grossAmount` (recommended): all-in. The Woovi fee comes OUT of it, so the account
    is debited exactly `grossAmount` and the provider is paid the remainder.
  - `value` (legacy): the amount paid to the provider, with the Woovi fee charged ON
    TOP — the account is debited `value` + `wooviFee`.

Either way the response breaks the total down into `wooviFee` and `providerFee`, and
`GET /api/v1/stablecoin/quote` reports the same numbers for the same input.

The deposit is always credited to the stable subaccount of the CompanyBankAccount
linked to the authenticated AppID. The AppID must have a `companyBankAccount`
configured (otherwise `400 APPLICATION_COMPANY_BANK_ACCOUNT_MISSING`), and that bank
account must have a stable subaccount in `CONFIRMED` status (a completed KYB) —
another bank account's subaccount on the same company is never used. Otherwise the
request is rejected with a `400`.

`subAccountId`, when sent, must belong to that same CompanyBankAccount.

Not every asset is available on every network. The supported matrix is:
  - USDT: POLYGON, ETHEREUM, CELO, TRON, BNB
  - USDC: POLYGON, ETHEREUM, BASE, CELO, BNB
  - BRLA: POLYGON, ETHEREUM, BASE, CELO

If `network` is omitted it defaults to `POLYGON`. Sending an asset/network combination
outside the matrix above returns a `400`.

Idempotency is supported via `correlationId`.

item.name: Read the monthly limits of the AppID sub-account, live from the provider

request.name: Read the monthly limits of the AppID sub-account, live from the provider

description.content:
Returns the monthly limits the provider (Avenia) enforces on the stable
sub-account linked to the authenticated Application's `companyBankAccount`,
read **live** at request time — not a copy stored by Woovi. For each entry
you get the ceiling (`limit`), how much of it this month already consumed
(`used`) and what is left (`remaining`), split by direction: `fiatIn`
(Pix → stable deposits), `fiatOut` (stable → Pix payouts), `chainIn` and
`chainOut` (on-chain transfers).

**Units.** Every amount is an integer in the minor unit (cents) of the
entry's `currency` — `10000000` in a `BRL` entry is R$ 100.000,00. The
entry with `scope: GLOBAL` is the provider's account-wide ceiling,
expressed in USD cents; `scope: CURRENCY` entries apply to that currency
only. `limit` and `remaining` are `null` when the provider reports no
ceiling for that direction. `year`/`month` identify the month `used`
refers to.

`blocked: true` means the provider has blocked every operation on this
sub-account because of its limits.

To raise the monthly limit use `POST /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/request`.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_LIST` scope.

**Choosing the sub-account.** `subAccountId` is optional. Sent, it is the sub-account
the call runs on; omitted, the one linked to the AppID's `companyBankAccount` answers.
You may name the sub-account of that bank account, or of another OPEN account of the
same company under the same taxID. Any other id is refused with
`400 STABLE_SUBACCOUNT_NOT_ALLOWED`. `GET /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/list` lists
the ids you can use.

query.description: Sub-account this call runs on. Optional — the one linked to the AppID bank account answers when omitted. Must belong to that bank account or to another OPEN account of the same company under the same taxID, otherwise 400 STABLE_SUBACCOUNT_NOT_ALLOWED.

item.name: Get a pre-signed URL to upload a limit-increase document

request.name: Get a pre-signed URL to upload a limit-increase document

description.content:
Step 1 of the monthly limit-increase flow: returns a pre-signed URL to
upload one supporting document (comprovante) — proof of financial
capacity, company address proof or UBO (partner) address proof.

The file goes straight from the client to storage; it never transits the
API. The URL is scoped to a key that belongs to the authenticated company,
is single use and expires in `expiresIn` seconds.

Upload it with `PUT <uploadUrl>` sending the same `Content-Type` returned
in `headers` and the raw file as the body — no multipart, no extra
headers. Then post the returned `document` object on
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/request` (or on
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/request/{limitRequestId}/document`).

Files above `maxSizeBytes`, or whose content type is not one of
`application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, are rejected
when the document is attached to the request.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_CREATE` scope and the company
`STABLECOIN` feature.

item.name: Request a higher monthly stablecoin limit

request.name: Request a higher monthly stablecoin limit

description.content:
Step 2 of the monthly limit-increase flow: opens the request with the
supporting documents (comprovantes) already uploaded through
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/document`.

Each document is checked before the request is persisted: it must live in
the company's own storage prefix, must actually have been uploaded, must
be within the size ceiling and must carry an accepted content type.

The push to the KYB provider runs in the background — the response comes
back with `submissionStatus: PROCESSING`. Poll
`GET /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/request/{limitRequestId}` until it flips to
`SENT` or `FAILED`.

The request raises the ceiling of the account the AppID answers for
(`companyBankAccountId` in the response). A company that holds several
accounts — a BaaS partner holds one per sub-merchant, each with its own
KYB — asks for each one separately, with that account's AppID.

`IN_REVIEW`, extra documents go to
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/limit/request/{limitRequestId}/document`. The
ceiling itself is raised by the analysis team once the documents are
approved — a successful call does not change the limit by itself.

`STABLECOIN` feature and a confirmed stablecoin subaccount.

item.name: List payouts, or get one by correlationId

request.name: List payouts, or get one by correlationId

description.content:
With `correlationId`, returns the single payout created under that
idempotency key — the same body as
`GET /api/v1/stablecoin/payout/{payoutId}`.

Without it, lists the authenticated company's payouts, newest first.

The list is served from storage: unlike the single-payout call it does not
re-read the provider ticket, so a payout still in flight is as fresh as the
last webhook or status read. Read an individual payout to force a sync.

`isRefunded` tells a settled payout that came back from one that did not.
A returned payout keeps `status: COMPLETED` — the Pix did leave — so the
status alone never reveals the return. Whether the money is usable again is
`refund.status` (`CONFIRMED` = spendable, `FAILED` = needs reconciliation),
not the flag.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_PAYOUT_CREATE` scope.

Only payouts created at or before this ISO date.

since past that MongoDB walks the index for every skipped document.

item.name: Pay out INTERNAL balance to BRL via Pix

request.name: Pay out INTERNAL balance to BRL via Pix

description.content:
Converts a stablecoin balance held on the company's INTERNAL float into
BRL and sends it to the given Pix key. Supported debit assets:
`USDT`, `USDC`, `BRLA`.

`value` is the **target Pix amount in BRL cents** (ex.: `10000` = R$ 100,00).
The INTERNAL debit in `currency` is taken from the provider quote.
The subaccount is resolved from the Application's `companyBankAccount`,
same as the wallets endpoint.

Flow (same two-step pattern as deposit): quote (fixed BRL) → balance
check → consume Woovi **OUT** limit (BRL cents) → resolve Pix beneficiary
→ persist as `PENDING`. Call `POST /api/v1/stablecoin/payout/approve` to
open the provider ticket and move to `PROCESSING`.

Fund the INTERNAL float first via
`GET /api/v1/stablecoin/wallets` (send USDT/USDC/BRLA on-chain to a returned
address), then call this endpoint.

Idempotency is supported via `correlationId`: reusing one returns the payout
already created for it.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_PAYOUT_CREATE` scope.

item.name: Get a stablecoin quote without creating a deposit

request.name: Get a stablecoin quote without creating a deposit

description.content:
Returns a PIX (BRL) -> stablecoin quote without creating a deposit, broken down into
BOTH fees: the Woovi fee (priced from the AppID bank account's stable deposit fee
settings, including its configured minimum) and the provider fee. Use it to display
the exact amount of stablecoin the customer would receive, and the exact BRL that
leaves the account, before confirming.

The amount field you send picks the fee model, exactly as in
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/deposit`:
  - `grossAmount` (recommended): all-in. The Woovi fee comes OUT of it, so
    `grossAmount` is what the account is debited and `inputAmount` is what the
    provider is quoted over.
  - `value` (legacy): the amount paid to the provider, with the Woovi fee charged ON
    TOP — the account is debited `grossAmount` = `value` + `wooviFee`.

BRL-denominated assets (BRLA) are charged the configured MINIMUM Woovi fee only: the
percentage is meaningless against a BRL value, so it never scales with the amount.

The AppID must have a `companyBankAccount` configured, otherwise the fee cannot be
priced and the request is rejected with `400
APPLICATION_COMPANY_BANK_ACCOUNT_MISSING`. A quote is never returned without the
Woovi fee — that would under-report what the customer pays.

The provider leg is cached for 60 seconds.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_DEPOSIT_CREATE` scope.

query.description:
Legacy model: amount paid to the provider, in cents (BRL), with the Woovi fee
charged on top. Send this or `grossAmount`, never both.

All-in model: total to debit, in cents (BRL). The Woovi fee comes out of it. Send
this or `value`, never both.
Stablecoin to receive. Defaults to USDT.

Requests a stablecoin subaccount (KYB) for the company behind your AppID,
reusing the KYC data already on its account register.

**The body can be empty** — the target account is resolved from the
credentials. Send `accountRegisterId` only to target another account
register of the same company (a BaaS partner asking for one of its
sub-merchants), and `companyBankAccountId` only to override which account
the subaccount is stamped with.

Every gate runs before the response, so `status` is the verdict:

| `status` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `IN_REVIEW` | Accepted. The outcome arrives as a `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_CONFIRMED` or `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_REJECTED` webhook. |
| `AWAITING_DOCUMENTS` | Documents are missing. Send the merchant to `rfi.url`; answering it re-runs the KYB. |
| `REJECTED` | Refused for good — screening, fraud markers, a CNPJ that is not ACTIVE, a refused KYC score. `reasonCode` says which. |
| `FAILED` | Blocked by a gap in the account register that only a Woovi operator can fix. Retrying does not help. |

Repeat calls are idempotent on the resolved account register: they return
the existing subaccount with its current verdict (HTTP `200`, including an
RFI link that is still open) instead of creating a duplicate. The first,
creating call returns HTTP `201`.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_CREATE` scope and the company
`STABLECOIN` feature.

item.name: Read the KYB USD (fiat rail) state of the company subaccount

request.name: Read the KYB USD (fiat rail) state of the company subaccount

description.content:
Status of the USD rail on the company's `CONFIRMED` stablecoin subaccount:
how far its KYB USD got and whether the provider currently accepts a USD
ticket for it.

Poll this after `POST /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/kyb/usd` — the
submission only creates the attempt, and the verdict lands later. While
the attempt can still change verdict the stored status is reconciled with
the provider on every read, so a rejection shows up here as soon as the
provider has it.

`usdUnlocked` is the field that actually gates the rail: an `APPROVED`
attempt alone is not enough, and it never turns true in the provider
sandbox.

The KYB USD is submitted on top of the Proof of Financial Capacity
attempt without waiting for its verdict; while the provider refuses the
submission the rail stays `PROOF_OF_FINANCIAL_CAPACITY_PENDING` and the
worker retries on a schedule. `usdKyb.proofOfFinancialCapacity` reports
that attempt on its own — when it was last read, when the next retry is
due, how long the wait may last and when it cleared — so a healthy wait
is never indistinguishable from a rail that was abandoned.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_LIST` scope and the company

item.name: Submit KYB USD (fiat rail) for a confirmed stablecoin subaccount

request.name: Submit KYB USD (fiat rail) for a confirmed stablecoin subaccount

description.content:
Unlocks the USD fiat rail on a company stablecoin subaccount that already has
KYB Level 1 approved (`StableSubAccount.status = CONFIRMED`).

The call **accepts** the submission and hands it to a worker: it answers
`202` right away and the provider work happens off the request path. That
work is uploading the supporting documents, opening the Proof of
Financial Capacity attempt, optionally submitting a company Proof of
Address, and submitting the KYB USD attempt on top of the Proof of
Financial Capacity — without waiting for that attempt to be `APPROVED`.
Uploading a Proof of Financial Capacity on its own never reaches the
provider's review; the KYB USD submission is what puts the subaccount in
front of it, and the provider judges both there.

It is still asynchronous: the provider may refuse the KYB USD while the
Proof of Financial Capacity is undecided, and the worker retries the
submission on a schedule for days, far past any HTTP gateway timeout.
Poll `GET /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/kyb/usd` for the outcome — the
rail reports `PROOF_OF_FINANCIAL_CAPACITY_PENDING` from the moment this
call is accepted, `PENDING` once the KYB USD attempt is created, and
finally `APPROVED` or `REJECTED`.

The call is idempotent. The queued job is keyed by the sub-account, and
the Proof of Financial Capacity attempt is claimed on the sub-account
itself, so posting twice converges on the submission already running
instead of opening a second provider attempt or re-uploading documents.
A repeat POST answers `202` with the same `jobId`, and the payload of the
submission already running is the one that counts.

Each document is sent in one of two forms.

**Preferred — upload it first.** Call
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/kyb/usd/document` for a pre-signed
URL, `PUT` the file to it, and post the returned `document` object back
here. The file never has to be exposed publicly, and the reference is
validated (ownership, size, content type) before any provider call runs.

**Or hand over a link.** The `*Url` fields still work and take a publicly
fetchable (or pre-signed) HTTPS link to the PDF/image. A reference wins
when both forms are sent for the same document.

**Several files for the same document.** Every reference field also takes
a list. The provider verifies one document per attempt and reuses the
attempt a subaccount already has, so extra files cannot be extra
attempts — the first entry is the one the provider is told about, and the
rest are uploaded to the subaccount document store, where the analyst
reviewing the attempt reads them. At most 10 files per document.

Required documents:
- `proofOfFinancialCapacity` / `proofOfFinancialCapacityUrl` — proof of
  financial capacity (PoFC)
- `proofOfRevenue` / `proofOfRevenueUrl` — proof of revenue

Optional documents:
- `proofOfAddressCompany` / `proofOfAddressCompanyUrl` — company proof of
  address (raises limits; independent of the USD rail, but accepted in the
  same call)

Also required:
- `businessType` — Bridge business type enum
- `businessIndustries` — at least one industry from the
  `StablecoinSubAccountKybUsdIndustry` enum (e.g. `SOFTWARE`; `OTHER`
  when none fits)
- `website` — required only when the company website was not captured at
  KYB Level 1

The subaccount must belong to the authenticated company and be `CONFIRMED`.
Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_CREATE` scope and the company
`STABLECOIN` feature.

Note: USD fiat rails are not available in the provider sandbox — submission
may appear to succeed, but `usdUnlocked` will not become true there.

item.name: Get a pre-signed URL to upload a KYB USD supporting document

request.name: Get a pre-signed URL to upload a KYB USD supporting document

description.content:
Step 1 of the USD fiat rail submission: returns a pre-signed URL to upload
one supporting document — proof of revenue, proof of financial capacity or
company proof of address.

The file goes straight from the client to storage; it never transits the
API. The URL is scoped to a key that belongs to the authenticated company,
is single use and expires in `expiresIn` seconds.

Upload it with `PUT <uploadUrl>` sending the same `Content-Type` returned
in `headers` and the raw file as the body — no multipart, no extra
headers. Then post the returned `document` object on
`POST /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/kyb/usd` as `proofOfRevenue`,
`proofOfFinancialCapacity` or `proofOfAddressCompany`.

This is the preferred way to send the documents: the `*Url` fields of the
submission need a publicly fetchable link, which means exposing the
company's financial documents on the open internet.

Files above `maxSizeBytes`, or whose content type is not one of
`application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, are rejected
when the document is attached to the submission.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SUBACCOUNT_CREATE` scope and the company
`STABLECOIN` feature.

item.name: Swap a stablecoin asset, optionally delivering it on-chain

request.name: Swap a stablecoin asset, optionally delivering it on-chain

description.content:
Converts a balance from one stablecoin asset into another on the company's
Avenia (sub-)account. Supported assets: `BRLA`, `USDC`, `USDT`.

`value` is the amount spent from the source (`from`) asset balance, in cents.

**Two output modes, one provider ticket either way:**

- Without `network` / `destinationWalletAddress` — an
  `INTERNAL -> INTERNAL` conversion. The output stays as a balance on the
  sub-account. `from` and `to` must be different assets.
- With both — an `INTERNAL -> <network>` ticket: the output is delivered
  on-chain to `destinationWalletAddress` instead of being credited to the
  balance. There is no second call and no second fee: the conversion and
  the delivery are quoted and settled as one ticket. In this mode `from`
  and `to` may be the same asset, which makes the request a plain
  on-chain payout with no conversion.

The two fields are only meaningful together — sending one without the
other is a `400`.

When the subaccount has `enforceWalletWhitelist` on, an on-chain
`destinationWalletAddress` must be an approved `(network, address)` pair;
the request is rejected before any limit is consumed or any provider call
is made. An INTERNAL-only swap moves nothing off-platform and is not
gated by the whitelist.

The company must have a stable subaccount in `CONFIRMED` status (a completed
KYB). Otherwise the request is rejected with a `400`.

Idempotency is supported via `correlationId`: reusing one returns the swap
already created for it instead of creating a second provider ticket. Always
send one when delivering on-chain — without it a retry sends the funds twice.

Requires the `STABLECOIN_SWAP_CREATE` scope.

item.name: List custodian deposit wallets for the AppID bank account

request.name: List custodian deposit wallets for the AppID bank account

description.content:
Returns the deposit addresses for the stable sub-account linked to the
authenticated Application's `companyBankAccount` (live from the provider —
not stored in Mongo).

A company can have more than one bank account / KYB sub-account. The
sub-account is resolved from `Application.companyBankAccount` (the
account bound to the AppID), not from the company alone.

Sending an asset on-chain to one of these addresses credits the INTERNAL
float used by `POST /api/v1/stablecoin/payout` (USDT/USDC/BRLA → Pix).

For an explicit provider id use
`GET /api/v1/stablecoin/subaccount/{subAccountId}/wallets`.
To read the float balance after funding use

Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Sends a TED from the account of the application behind the AppID or, when
the application has none, from the company's default account: the same
account a Pix out is paid from. The body cannot choose it. The response means the TED was
accepted for processing — it settles when the BACEN answers, and the
`TED_OUT_CONFIRMED` / `TED_OUT_REJECTED` webhooks say which way it went.

Retrying with the same `correlationID` is safe: it returns the TED that
already exists, without a second debit and without a second STR request.

The TED settles on the day it is sent (Brasília time). It cannot be
scheduled: while the STR is closed it is refused with `422`
`OUTSIDE_STR_SESSION`.

Returns a TED your company received to its sender, for the full value.
The response is the refund TED (`type: TED_REFUND_SENT`)
accepted for processing — it settles when the BACEN answers, and the
`TED_REFUND_SENT_CONFIRMED` webhook says it did. The received TED is
`REFUNDED` from then on. If the BACEN rejects it, `TED_REFUND_SENT_REJECTED`
says so and the received TED stays `COMPLETED`, so it can be refunded again.

Only a `TED_IN` can be refunded: not a TED you sent, and not a
refund you received. Retrying while the refund is still in flight is safe:
it returns the same refund, without a second debit.

item.name: Get the public keys that verify the webhook signature

request.name: Get the public keys that verify the webhook signature

description.content:
Retorna a chave pública usada para verificar o header `x-webhook-signature`, presente em todo webhook enviado pela Woovi.

A assinatura é `base64(RSA-SHA256)` sobre o corpo **bruto** da request — verifique antes de fazer parse do JSON, porque reserializar muda os bytes e invalida a assinatura.

Este endpoint **não exige autenticação**: a chave é pública por definição, e quem recebe webhook normalmente valida a assinatura em um contexto que não tem o AppID em mãos.

A resposta é uma lista, e não uma chave só, para permitir rotação: durante uma troca de chave publicamos a antiga e a nova ao mesmo tempo, com `is_current` indicando qual está assinando agora. Aceite qualquer chave da lista ao verificar e você não quebra quando a rotação acontecer.

description.content:
A Woovi é uma Plataforma de Gestão de Pagamentos. 

 Para utilizar nossa API de Produção, utilize exclusivamente o seguinte endpoint: 

 👉 __[https://api.woovi.com/](https://api.woovi.com/)__ 

 Além disso, oferecemos também um ambiente de sandbox (ambiente de testes), ideal para desenvolvimento e validação de integrações sem impactar dados reais. 

 👉 __[https://api.woovi-sandbox.com/](https://api.woovi-sandbox.com/)__ 

 Veja como configurar seu acesso a nossa API [aqui](https://developers.woovi.com/docs/apis/api-getting-started).
